subtitle: Open or paste JSON to browse it as a collapsible tree with types, array indexes and copyable paths; nothing is uploaded.
intro: A free JSON tree viewer: open a .json file, drop it or paste the text, and it opens as a tree with the top two levels expanded. Fold and unfold any object or array, search keys and values, and copy the path of any node, such as data.items[3].price, to use in your code. Arrays of objects can be shown as a table, and on a wide screen the formatted text sits beside the tree. The file is read in your browser and never leaves your device.

stepsTitle: How it works: view JSON as a tree

steps.title: Open or paste your JSON
steps.text: Choose a .json file, drop it on the page, paste the text into the box, or try one of the two samples.

steps.title: Browse the tree
steps.text: The top two levels open expanded. Click an object or array to fold or unfold it, or use Expand all and Collapse all.

steps.title: Find and copy
steps.text: Search for a key or value to jump to it, then copy the node's path. Arrays of objects can switch to a table.

handlesTitle: What the JSON tree viewer handles
handles: A collapsible tree with the top two levels expanded, plus Expand all and Collapse all.
The type of every value (string, number, boolean, null, object, array) and the index of every array item.
Search across keys and values, with each match shown in the tree.
Copy a node's path, such as data.items[3].price.
A table view for arrays of objects, and the formatted text beside the tree on wide screens.
Big integer IDs shown with every digit.
limits: The tree needs valid JSON; a file with a syntax error opens in the text pane with the error marked.
The table view is for arrays of objects; other arrays stay in the tree.
faqTitle: Questions about the JSON tree viewer

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your JSON is read and drawn as a tree by your browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. Pasted text stays in this tab. Your browser's network panel shows no upload.

faq.question: How do I get the path to a value?
faq.answer: Select the node in the tree and choose Copy path. You get a path such as data.items[3].price, with dots for keys and brackets for array indexes, ready to paste into your code.

faq.question: Why are only two levels open?
faq.answer: So a large document stays readable when it opens. Click any node to go deeper, or press Expand all to open everything at once.

faq.question: Can I see an array of records as a table?
faq.answer: Yes. An array whose items are objects can be shown as a table, one row per item and one column per key.

faq.question: How large a file can the tree show?
faq.answer: Files up to 10 MB. Larger files are refused before they are read, so the page stays responsive.

faq.question: Will long numbers be shown correctly?
faq.answer: Yes. Integers too long for JavaScript, such as 64-bit IDs, are shown and copied with every digit, not rounded.

faq.question: How do I view a JSON file as a tree?
faq.answer: Open or paste the JSON in OpenAnyDoc's JSON tree viewer: objects and arrays fold and unfold, the top two levels start open, and search jumps to any key or value. The file is read in your browser without being uploaded.

faq.question: Which app can open a JSON file?
faq.answer: Any text editor opens a .json file: Notepad on Windows, TextEdit on a Mac, or a code editor, and every web browser shows it as text. A tree viewer makes a large or nested one easier to read. More ways are in the guide on how to open a JSON file.
